title: Bond Market Turning Point: Why Jim Bianco Just Flipped After 5 Years
speaker: Jim Bianco (Bianco Research), interviewed by David Lin

macro_themes.theme: Bonds near a peak in yield
macro_themes.view: After being short since 2020, sees real value in bonds with the 10y ~5.2%; bearish narratives are largely priced in.
Warsh must choose between the president's wrath (hike) and the bond market's wrath (no hike); a skipped hike could send long rates up a lot.
Goods inflation structurally higher from tariffs/deglobalization; Fed's '2% year after next' forecast unrealistic; higher-rate world going forward.
5% yields are normal; expect cash 4%, bonds 5%, stocks 6%; bonds will siphon some money from equities.

calls.reason: Yields near peak with bearish inflation/deficit narratives priced in; 5.5% IG yields are compelling on a risk-adjusted basis.
calls.quote: I would and actually am starting to look towards getting long the bond market.

calls.condition: An Iran/Hormuz deal could bring yields into the high 4s, but not the low 4s
calls.reason: Believes ~5.2% on the 10y may be close to a peak; risk of further spike if Fed skips an expected hike.
calls.quote: I'm not going to be, you know, smart enough to say 525 is the high. Uh, but we're getting close enough

calls.reason: Still largely risk-on near all-time highs; market will accept 5.25-5.5% yields as normal, though expects only ~6% stock returns.
calls.quote: I would say that we're still largely in a risk-on environment.

calls.reason: Failure of the Clarity Act is good for crypto as a disruptive force; concern it still trades with stocks.
calls.quote: I'm actually bullish that the Clarity Act didn't pass on Bitcoin.

notes: Host states 'today is Monday, September 28th'. Bianco's index ETF WTBN mentioned (self-promotion, not recorded). Oil 'effective price ~$200' framing, no directional oil call.
